tests.title: Unit 6: Rectification of Errors – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: An error in accounting is:
options: A mistake in recording, classifying or summarising transactions
questions.explanation: It can be clerical or one of principle.

questions.question_text: The main types of errors are:
options: Errors of omission, commission, principle and compensating errors
questions.explanation: Others: errors of original entry, duplication and casting.

questions.question_text: A complete omission differs from a partial omission in that in a complete omission:
options: The transaction is not recorded at all, while in a partial omission only one aspect is omitted
questions.explanation: Complete omission does not affect the trial balance.

questions.question_text: An error of commission is an error:
options: Made while recording or posting, e.g., posting to a wrong account

questions.question_text: An error of principle occurs when:
options: The accounting principle is violated, e.g., capital expenditure treated as revenue

questions.question_text: Compensating errors are:
options: Errors that cancel out each other's effect
questions.explanation: E.g., two accounts overstated and understated by the same amount.

questions.question_text: An error of original entry is when:
options: A wrong amount is entered in the book of original entry
questions.explanation: Both aspects use the wrong figure.

questions.question_text: An error of duplication is:
An error of casting is:
options: A mistake in adding up the totals

questions.question_text: Which errors do not affect the trial balance?
options: Complete omission, errors of principle, compensating errors and errors of original entry
questions.explanation: Debit and credit totals remain equal.

questions.question_text: Which errors affect the trial balance?
options: One-sided errors such as casting, balancing and posting errors

questions.question_text: One-sided errors affect:
options: Only one account (debit or credit), disturbing the trial balance

questions.question_text: If the trial balance does not agree, the first step to locate the error is to:
options: Recheck the totals and balances of accounts, then the postings

questions.question_text: A transposition error is where digits are interchanged; the difference is always:
questions.explanation: E.g., 54 written as 45 gives a difference of 9.

questions.question_text: A slide error is:
options: Shifting the decimal or digit places, e.g., 500 written as 5,000

questions.question_text: A difference equal to half of the amount of an error suggests:
options: The amount was posted on the wrong side
questions.explanation: A wrong-side posting causes a difference of twice the amount.

questions.question_text: A suspense account is:
options: A temporary account to carry a trial balance difference until errors are found

questions.question_text: A suspense account is opened to:
options: Make the trial balance agree when the difference cannot be located

questions.question_text: When the debit side of the trial balance is short, the suspense account is placed on the:
The suspense account is closed by:
options: Rectifying errors using it, until its balance becomes nil

questions.question_text: A remaining suspense balance is shown in the final accounts on:
options: The balance sheet (assets if debit, liabilities if credit)
questions.explanation: It is treated as a balance sheet item until located.

questions.question_text: Errors are rectified:
options: Before the preparation of final accounts or after

questions.question_text: The steps in rectification are:
options: Identify the error, find the correct entry, and pass a rectifying entry
questions.explanation: Pass the entry to correct the effect.

questions.question_text: The Profit and Loss Adjustment Account is used when:
options: Errors are rectified after the final accounts have been prepared and profit is affected
questions.explanation: Its balance is transferred to capital.

questions.question_text: Compensating errors are difficult to detect because:
Internal controls reduce errors by:
options: Checks, authorisation and segregation of duties

questions.question_text: A suspense account has a nil balance after full rectification because:
options: All errors that created the difference have been corrected

questions.question_text: A transaction error can occur without any suspense entry, for example:
options: An error of principle (the trial balance agrees)
questions.explanation: Suspense is for trial balance differences only.

questions.question_text: Computerised systems reduce errors by:
Rectification before final accounts is done by:
options: Correcting accounts directly, while after final accounts it uses the P&L Adjustment Account

questions.question_text: The auditor's role is to:
options: Examine records and detect errors and frauds
questions.explanation: The auditor reports on true and fair view.

questions.question_text: An error differs from a fraud in that an error is:
options: Unintentional, while a fraud is deliberate

questions.question_text: A two-sided error that does not require a suspense account is:
options: Goods purchased from X credited to Y

questions.question_text: Rectification of one-sided errors requires suspense because:
options: The trial balance does not agree and a suspense balance was created earlier
questions.explanation: Suspense is used to clear it.
